title: Weather Web Page
intro: Show the temperature and humidity on a web page anyone in the room can open.

wiring_steps.title: The temperature sensor
wiring_steps.text: Unplug the USB cable before you change any wires. Plug it back in when you're done. Start with the power rails: a black wire from GND on your board to the blue (−) rail at the bottom of the breadboard, and a red wire from {{VCC}} to the red (+) rail. Push the DHT sensor's three pins into J10, J11 and J12: S (data) in J10, + in J11, − in J12. Add a wire from {{pin:DHT_PIN}} to G10, a red wire from F11 to the red (+) rail, and a black wire from F12 to the blue (−) rail.

steps.title: Read the sensor
steps.text:
The DHT sensor measures temperature and humidity (how much water is in the air). It's slow: read it every 2 seconds at most.

**Your task:** Run, open the **Serial Monitor**, then breathe on the sensor and watch the numbers change.
hints: `isnan` means "is not a number": the reading failed.
In the simulator, drag the temperature and humidity sliders.
If you see "No reading", check the data wire and the 3.3V and GND wires.

checks.label: The numbers change when I breathe on it

steps.title: The weather page
steps.text:
Now the board builds a web page with the readings. The page is a **String**, built up piece by piece with `+=`. `String(t, 1)` turns the temperature into text with 1 decimal place.

Your board makes its **own WiFi network** (a hotspot). On your phone, open WiFi settings, join the network with your board's name, then open **192.168.4.1** in the browser. In the simulator, use the **phone panel**.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks to add the readings to the page.

checks.label: I saw the weather on a phone (or the phone panel)

steps.success: Anyone who joins your board's WiFi can check the weather.

steps.title: Your own design
steps.text: **Goal:** make the page your own: a title with your name, the temperature in a big coloured box, and a line that says `Hot!` above 25 °C, `Cold!` below 15 °C, or `Just right` otherwise.
hints: Use `if`, `else if` and `else` to choose the message.
Add the message to `page` before the closing `</body></html>`.
CSS like `background: orange; padding: 20px` makes a coloured box.
steps.success: A weather web page designed by you.

outro: Your weather station is on the web! The board reads the **DHT** sensor and builds a fresh **HTML** page with the numbers every time someone asks for it.
stretch: Make the page refresh itself every 5 seconds (look up the meta refresh tag).
Show the highest temperature since the board started.
Change the page's background colour when it's hot.
